topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Concept of 'Perspective' (Prerequisite Review)
sections.content: Define a basis as a coordinate system (a set of rulers). Explain that the same point in space can be described by different numbers depending on which 'rulers' we use. Visual: An animation of a 2D plane showing a point P with coordinates (2, 3) relative to standard grid lines, then shifting the grid lines.
sections.example: Imagine a cat sitting on a rug. If you measure its position relative to the room's corner (Basis A), it's (2, 2). If you measure it relative to the rug's corner (Basis B), it's (1, 1).

sections.title: The Transition Matrix (The Bridge)
sections.content: Introduce the Change of Basis matrix (P). Explain that P acts as a 'translator' that converts coordinates from the new basis to the old basis (or vice versa). Visual: An animated flow chart where a vector v in Basis B is 'multiplied' by matrix P to emerge as the same vector in Basis A.
sections.example: A GPS device uses WGS84 coordinates. To show the location on a local city map (a different basis), the device multiplies the global coordinates by a specific transition matrix.

sections.title: Deriving the Calculation Process
sections.content: Show the formal equation: [v]_A = P * [v]_B. Explain that P is composed of columns representing the basis vectors of B written in terms of Basis A. Visual: A split-screen showing vectors b1 and b2 being broken down into components of standard basis e1 and e2.
sections.example: If Basis B = { (1,1), (0,1) }, the matrix P = [[1, 0], [1, 1]]. Mapping a point (2, 3) from B to A becomes a simple matrix multiplication.

sections.title: Practical Application & Summary
sections.content: Briefly mention that choosing the 'right' basis can simplify complex problems (like diagonalization). Recap: Change of basis doesn't change the vector, just our description of it. Visual: A complex rotation problem where the math looks messy in the standard basis but becomes a simple scaling operation in a rotated basis.
sections.example: A robot arm (character) rotates its 'hand' to grab an object. By changing the basis to the hand's orientation, the calculation for the grasp becomes trivial compared to calculating it from the floor's perspective.
